sections.title: BL-003 — the helper works on a stock Windows install
sections.need: Nothing beyond git and node on PATH. No test data, no credentials, no network access. These two steps read configuration; they change none.

steps.do:
Run git config --system --name-only --get-regexp "^filter\..*\.(clean|process)$". Then run this, which inspects every tracked and untracked path and reports only the answer:

node -e "const {execSync}=require('child_process');const out=execSync('git ls-files -z --cached --others --exclude-standard | git check-attr filter -z --stdin',{shell:true,maxBuffer:64e6}).toString();const f=out.split('�');if(f[f.length-1]==='')f.pop();let p=0,bad=[];for(let i=0;i+2<=f.length;i+=3){p++;const v=f[i+2];if(v!=='unspecified'&&v!=='unset')bad.push(f[i]+' -> '+v);}console.log('paths inspected:',p);console.log('paths resolving to a filter:',bad.length);if(bad.length)console.log(bad.join(' '));"
steps.pass: The first lists filter.lfs.clean and filter.lfs.process — stock Git for Windows. The second reports a non-zero paths inspected and paths resolving to a filter: 0. If any path did resolve, it is named.
steps.aside: Runner: agent, pre-verified — 375 paths inspected, 0 resolving. This is the exact situation BL-003 describes: a filter driver configured machine-wide that no file actually uses. The old code refused on the first fact alone, which is why the helper was unusable on every stock Windows install; the new code asks the second question. If the first command returns nothing, this machine has no LFS filter configured and the canary proves less than it should — say so rather than recording a pass. This is the claim no test in the suite can make, because every fixture sets GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 and an empty global config precisely to isolate your real configuration away. The raw pipeline prints one record per path — 1,125 NUL-separated fields here — which is why this step summarises instead.

steps.do: Run the full validation recipe (Section 4, Step 8), then find these three tests in its output: configured clean and process filters never execute through API or actual CLI status probes, global clean filters remain unknown and never execute through API or actual CLI, and configured filters leave the fence UNKNOWN without executing a command or changing bytes.
steps.pass: All three pass. One unit = one named test; expect three.
steps.aside: Runner: agent, pre-verified. This is the refusal half of the fix. A helper that stopped refusing when a path does resolve to a filter would have stopped protecting anything — the point was to narrow the trigger, not remove it. An independent gate confirmed these still bind by mutating the new code to always return safe: all three went red.

sections.title: BL-004, BL-005, BL-006 — the agent-definition guards
sections.need: Nothing beyond the repository. Step 6 creates and then deletes one untracked file; it never touches the four tracked definitions and never writes into your ~/.claude/agents/.

steps.do: Create .claude/agents/subdir/orchestrator.md containing the single line hello. Run the validation recipe. Then delete the file and the subdir directory and re-run.
steps.pass: RED with the failure naming the directory holds exactly the four known definitions and the path subdir/orchestrator.md; green after the delete, with git status --porcelain empty.
steps.aside: Runner: agent, pre-verified — it went red on exactly that test (259/1), then back to 260/0, and the four tracked definitions were hash-identical throughout. This is BL-005: the old whitelist listed one directory level, so a nested definition escaped it entirely and would ship with no tools: line, inheriting every tool.

steps.do: In the recipe's output, find the frontmatter case-table tests and the escape whitelist admits exactly the characters YAML defines.
steps.pass: The three forms BL-004 names each appear as their own passing case, the quoted-colon accept case appears, and the whitelist sweep passes.
steps.aside: Runner: agent, pre-verified. The sweep checks all 95 printable ASCII characters against the 18 escapes YAML defines, in both directions, with the member list written independently of the regex so that editing both at once is still caught. This batch took three review rounds and three polish passes because five separate times the fix for "an assertion that cannot fail" itself contained one; the sweep is what finally holds the boundary rather than sampling it.

steps.aside: Runner: agent, pre-verified. Base was 207, so this change adds 53 tests. node --test bare from the root is the portable equivalent; node --test tests/ is not — Node's directory-argument discovery differs and the suite fails. That distinction is itself documented in the README and pinned by a test.
